items.name: Live evidence and traps
items.behavior: pc.py small() raises OSError(28). Both --loop-small and --loop exit 1, with no restart supervisor and no node-local failure log in the original kit. The 600-second small loop cannot resume after space returns; a fresh manual small() succeeds. The final pass runs small first, so ENOSPC prevents its exports/stop checkpoint actions. EXIT preserves status 0; TERM/USR1 with a real fake-worker descendant save its local checkpoint and return 0. The no-worker signal tests return 143/138. pl.py is a pre-training publisher, not the periodic publisher.
items.fatal_detail: Not fatal to the independently running trainer; fatal to both publication workers. Trap finalization suppresses its failed publication commands.
items.data_loss_detail: Local source evidence survives. Remote evidence remains stale/missing; .part files can be empty, and direct copy.json writes can damage an old manifest. Node loss before a retry loses unpublished evidence.
items.retry: No automatic retry after the uncaught error. Manual recovery succeeds.
items.runtime_log: Original stderr goes to X/j through jn.sh and may itself be unwritable. Tests capture stderr on node-local disk.
items.fix: Proposed pc.py catches publication errors, logs to N/live_spool/retry.log and keeps its loops alive. jn2.sh separately retries screened wrapper log tails.

items.name: Stdout and stderr
items.behavior: The requested file-fd test makes Python print/flush exit 120. With the real l.py, the logger exits 120 on ENOSPC and the x.py-like printing child exits 120 on BrokenPipeError. Direct stderr flush also exits 120. The wrapper fix keeps both fds local: a 300-line child and l.py exit 0 and save a 4096-byte checkpoint; the helper records E28 and automatically publishes the exact 1694-byte tail after recovery.
items.fatal_detail: Yes for the tested printing child/logger. Actual trainer stdout is already redirected to N/t.log in the decoded shell; this test does not prove Slurm daemon buffering propagates ENOSPC to a real job.
items.data_loss_detail: Original stdout/stderr bytes that only target the full filesystem are lost. Under jn2.sh full local logs survive during allocation; published tails are intentionally bounded to 300000 bytes per stream.
items.retry: Original l.py has none. jn2.sh helper retries every 600 seconds; focused test uses its interval argument at 0.1 seconds.
items.runtime_log: Fixed N/j2.log, N/j2.err, N/j2.retry.log; Slurm bootstrap fds /tmp/q_22c714e1_%j.log/.err.
items.fix: out/jn2.sh changes only the wrapper and starts an independent log-tail publisher. It does not fix kit publication or GCS claims.

items.name: Pre-training receipts and review gate
items.behavior: The real rv.put write path raises OSError(28) for v.json, h0.json, c0..c4.json and s0/s1. Replayed sealed pl.py and h.py publication statements fail at their actual write sites. rv.run fails writing v.json, then fails again writing REVIEW_REFUSED.json. If space fills after WAITING_REVIEW is written, reads still work and a missing review reaches the deadline; the refusal write then also raises ENOSPC. No training admission is granted.
items.fatal_detail: Yes, before training; fail-closed admission is appropriate. The publication statements and review state machine were tested with synthetic prerequisites, not a full data preparation run.
items.data_loss_detail: Config/host sources remain node-local. Census keys may exist only in memory before a failed first publication, but can be recomputed; no training checkpoint exists at this phase. The independent review.json is read, never written by this job.
items.retry: No receipt-publication retry. The review poll retries reads only, up to the sealed 7200-second bound (scaled to 1 second in the focused test).
items.runtime_log: Most receipt exceptions go to N/q.log, N/h.log or N/rv.log; outer staging diagnostics can use wrapper stdout.
items.fix: Keep the gate fail-closed; reserve enough space or retry preparation with a fresh reviewed allocation. No bypass is proposed.

items.name: Checkpoints, stop checkpoint and exports
items.behavior: Native persistence produces node-local archives and durable=false receipts when X is full. The final config has r1_training and no r2_persistence. pc.py does not upload ordinary checkpoints at all; it uploads exports and the final stop checkpoint. A fresh export/stop upload fails on the project-side claim before gc.py runs. With a preexisting claim, real gc.py reaches the local fake HTTP sink (four verified parts), then the project done write fails. The free-space race also fails writing n_ck/...tar.part and never falls back to GCS. Direct gc.py with local sessions/receipts succeeds.
items.fatal_detail: The fake trainer continues, but the copier dies and durability fails. Upload failure is not a trainer exception in this kit.
items.data_loss_detail: No only local checkpoint/archive copy is deleted. Fresh-state GCS publication is blocked, so allocation loss would lose unuploaded states; ordinary checkpoints have no periodic GCS route in the original kit.
items.retry: Native local receipt persists. pc.py loop terminates when its error-status write also fails; no automatic restart. Recovery requires a new copier invocation.
items.runtime_log: N/p/q/r/persist and N/live_spool hold local archives. Writer receipts are N/live_spool/private/sess.json.receipts.jsonl. Original copier exceptions use the vulnerable batch stderr.
items.fix: Proposed sealed patch uses per-allocation GCS names, cached sessions, local claims/status/receipts, 16 ordinary-checkpoint slots and a dedicated stop object. No project write lies on the upload path. New sessions must be minted externally before launch; no network was used here.

items.name: Exit archive and diagnostics
items.behavior: o.py creates N/o/o.tar, then shutil.copyfile to X/o/<job>/o.tar raises OSError(28), exits 1 and skips creation of N/o/RESULT.json. The decoded shell has set +e and exits with the saved training rc, so the archive error does not change that rc. ep.py also exits 1; pc.sh suppresses it. After recovery, rerunning o.py succeeds.
items.fatal_detail: Fatal to the archive subprocess only; not to the saved job/training status.
items.data_loss_detail: The complete local o.tar survives. A remote partial tar may remain and RESULT.json is absent until retry. The archive is not uploaded to GCS by this kit, so node teardown before recovery can lose it.
items.retry: No original exit-archive retry. Proposed o.py retains RESULT locally, catches ENOSPC, logs locally and lets small publication retry while the allocation is alive; finalizer attempts again.
items.runtime_log: Original exception uses batch stderr. Fixed wrapper captures it locally; proposed archive retry log is N/o/retry.log.
items.fix: Proposed b/o.py and b/pc.py/b/pc.sh changes. No promise of retries after allocation teardown; durable exit-archive upload would require an additional separately provisioned object.

proposed_patch.scope: pc.py, pc.sh, o.py, k/y.json plus exact regenerated N kit manifest/BUILD only
prerequisites: Provision per-allocation sessions at X/n_s/sess_<job>.json with owner-private permissions before pc.sh --prepare. Keys are each k/y.json object + .j<job>, with four part suffixes. These are new resumable sessions, not reuse of prior objects.
The 26 labels require 104 session URLs (10 existing export/stop labels +16 ordinary-checkpoint slots). Stage the file before training; it is cached locally.
Regenerate affected N upload inventory/package pins and resolver receipt after applying/resealing. Other kits and tree stay unchanged.
Repeat independent kit/launch and object-allocation safety review; mint a fresh runtime review.json for the prepared config.

Redo the CPU preparation/discovery/admission job for the changed N kit, then a short four-GPU N launch that exercises TERM/USR1, checkpoints, exports and recovery before any 24-hour launch. No remote job was run here.
limits: This is a proposed, CPU-fixture-tested patch, not an approved deployable launch. Native admission, real GCS ownership/retry semantics, throughput and finalizer deadline require those reviews/jobs.
Exit archive remains node-local if X stays full through allocation teardown; no extra GCS archive object is proposed.
The 16 ordinary-checkpoint slots follow the sealed 14+2 disk plan; slot exhaustion is logged and needs review.
Project read failures, node-local ENOSPC and full inode exhaustion are outside this block-ENOSPC test.

card_sentences: ENOSPC gate: FAIL. The sealed N kit cannot guarantee durable state publication when X is full.
jn2.sh fixes the tested stdout/stderr failure outside the seal: local logging continues, E28 retries are local, and the same helper republishes after recovery.
The sealed copier exits on ENOSPC; new export and stop uploads require a project-side claim. Ordinary checkpoints have no periodic GCS route.
The proposed patch moves upload claims and receipts to local storage and requires fresh per-allocation GCS sessions, N resealing, review, and new CPU/admission plus short N validation jobs.

Observed pre-training live receipts total 36,436 bytes (s0=35,026; s1=1,410). The complete pre-training write total is unknown because the supplied outputs omit N admission receipts and log boundaries.
No sealed kit, tree, network service, scheduler job or GPU was changed or used by this test.
test_limits_and_failures: All mounts are private unshare -Urmn tmpfs mounts: 16 MiB initially, at most 64 MiB after recovery. dd exhausts blocks and df reports zero available. Recovery adds capacity with an explicit tmpfs remount; no filler/file deletion is used.

Exact copied kit files execute unchanged. Harness-only runtime mapping changes k/p.json n_root in memory. HTTP is replaced by an in-process local sink while real gc.py split/upload/hash/receipt code runs. The network namespace has no external connectivity.
Fake training supplies only small local steps/checkpoints. Full GPU training, full data preparation, scheduler and Slurm daemon I/O behavior were not run.

pl.py and h.py tests replay their exact AST publication statements; rv.put covers the same census receipt writer. rv.run tests replace identity/evidence prerequisites. Native persistence tests replace space-plan/complete-state prerequisites and use a zero reserve for small fixtures.

The first recovery command omitted the tmpfs source/type and failed with mount exit32; its full output is in work/enospc/attempt1/logs/recovery.log. The corrected explicit source/type remount succeeds.

The 10000-line, 1024-character-token wrapper stress fixture exceeded its 15-second screening timeout; its recovery probe ran too early. Those outputs remain in logs/wrapper_full_pipeline.log and logs/wrapper_recovered.log. The bounded 300-line test verifies successful completion and automatic recovery.

The first native export fixture reused the checkpoint marker bytes and received the existing local checkpoint receipt. The distinct-marker native_export_case.py test verifies an export archive/receipt separately; neither fixture is a real trained state.
